content.text: Both elements are present: California law and exclusive California courts, with no arbitration. This sits at the playbook fallback, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: 26. APPLICABLE LAW. This Agreement shall be governed, construed and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the State of California (without respect to principles of conflicts of law).
input.rationale: Contrary to the planner's assumption, governing law and venue do appear (§§ 26-27, paragraphs p0093-p0094, carried under the § 12 heading). Section 26 selects the laws of the State of California, and Section 27 designates the state or federal courts located in San Luis Obispo County, California as the sole and exclusive forum, with mutual consent to jurisdiction. California law with California courts sits squarely at the playbook fallback position (Delaware or California law and courts), so the clause is acceptable and is not redlined. Disputes go to courts rather than arbitration, and there is no foreign seat or foreign exclusive venue, so walk-away territory is not implicated. Two minor sub-elements short of the preferred position are noted but not flagged: the law is California rather than New York, and venue is fixed in San Luis Obispo County (the Vendor's local county) rather than New York County. Both are mutual and reciprocal in operation, and the related fee-shifting provision in § 28 likewise runs to the prevailing party of either side, so no term here operates one-way against us. If we are reopening other commercial points, we could ask to move the forum to a neutral major California venue, but that is a preference, not a fallback failure.
